faq.q: What is the origin of Israa?
faq.a: Israa is associated with Arabic. Israa is Arabic إِسْرَاء (Isrāʾ) 'night journey', the term for the Prophet's night journey and the title of a Qur'anic sura. The source gloss 'Night Journey' is consistent. Same name as isra and issra.
Yes — the underlying form إسراء is Arabic.
Israa can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Israa mean in Persian?

faq.a: Romanization variants include Israa, isra, israa. Script forms are إسراء, اسراء, इसरा.

faq.q: Is Israa a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
